title: How twist angle inhomogeneity masks the BKT transition and the order parameter symmetry
authors: Ilaria Maccari, Louk Rademaker, Giulia Venditti
abstract: Two-dimensional superconductors, including twisted multilayer graphene, should exhibit a BKT transition, and the $T$-dependence of the superfluid stiffness should distinguish between nodal or gapped order parameter symmetries. However, this picture dramatically changes when spatially correlated disorder is taken into account. Such correlations naturally arise in moiré systems due to twist angle inhomogeneities, which we model using elasticity theory. Using a random impedance network based on realistic disorder in the local $T_c$, we show that the finite-frequency conductance reveals a smeared percolative transition instead of a BKT transition. At low temperatures, the disorder can effectively obscure the distinction between nodal and fully gapped superconducting order parameters. We propose that the real part of the conductivity can be used as a key diagnostic observable to probe the relevance of correlated disorder.
summary: The paper demonstrates that spatially correlated disorder, inherent in moiré superconductors due to twist angle variations, fundamentally alters superconducting phase transitions. By modeling the system using a Random Impedance Network, the authors show that this correlation smears the BKT transition and masks intrinsic order parameter symmetries, suggesting $\sigma_1$ is the key diagnostic observable.
main_problem: The study investigates how spatially correlated disorder, arising from twist angle inhomogeneities in moiré superconductors, masks the expected Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless (BKT) transition. Furthermore, this disorder obscures the ability to distinguish between different superconducting order parameter symmetries.
main_result: Correlated disorder smears the sharp BKT transition into a smooth crossover and causes low-temperature superfluid stiffness to decay in a manner mimicking nodal pairing, regardless of the true symmetry.
method: The authors employ a Random Impedance Network (RIN) model built upon local critical temperatures ($T_{c,i}$) derived from elasticity theory describing twist angle variations. They compare these exact numerical results against simpler Effective Medium Theory (EMT) approximations.
model_or_system: The system is modeled as two-dimensional superconductors, specifically twisted multilayer graphene in a moiré pattern. Disorder is introduced via long-range correlated fluctuations in the local critical temperature ($T_{c,i}$), which are governed by elasticity theory and result in $\log|r|$ correlations for the twist angle.
